title: DSPy Program Optimizers (Teleprompters)
summary: This module provides a collection of advanced teleprompters (optimizers) for DSPy programs, enabling automated prompt engineering, few-shot example selection, and fine-tuning strategies. It includes techniques for iterative prompt refinement, evolutionary optimization, reinforcement learning-based fine-tuning, and meta-optimization.

nodes.label: Optimize Program Instructions
nodes.title: AvatarOptimizer
nodes.description: Iteratively refines a program's instructions by analyzing positive and negative execution examples and generating feedback-based updates.

nodes.label: Compare Program Performance
nodes.title: Comparator
nodes.description: Analyzes successful and unsuccessful program executions to identify patterns and provide feedback for instruction improvement.

nodes.label: Generate Improved Instructions
nodes.title: FeedbackBasedInstruction
nodes.description: Creates new, enhanced instructions for a program by incorporating specific feedback derived from performance analysis.

nodes.label: Combine Optimization Strategies
nodes.title: BetterTogether
nodes.description: A meta-optimizer that orchestrates sequences of prompt and weight optimization steps, allowing iterative improvement of DSPy programs.

nodes.label: Iteratively Optimize Prompts
nodes.title: COPRO
nodes.description: Optimizes program prompts (instructions and output prefixes) using a breadth-first search approach, iteratively refining them based on performance.

nodes.label: Generate Initial Instructions
nodes.title: BasicGenerateInstruction
nodes.description: Proposes a set of initial instructions and output field prefixes for a given task, serving as starting points for optimization.

nodes.label: Refine Instructions from Attempts
nodes.title: GenerateInstructionGivenAttempts
nodes.description: Generates improved instructions and prefixes by analyzing previous optimization attempts and their corresponding performance scores.

nodes.label: Evolve Prompts with Reflection
nodes.title: GEPA
nodes.description: An evolutionary optimizer that uses reflection to iteratively refine program instructions based on detailed feedback from execution traces.

nodes.label: Define Feedback Metric
nodes.title: GEPAFeedbackMetric
nodes.description: A protocol for defining custom metrics that provide both a score and textual feedback, crucial for guiding GEPA's reflective optimization process.

nodes.label: Propose Multimodal Instructions
nodes.title: MultiModalInstructionProposer
nodes.description: A GEPA-compatible component that proposes new instructions, specifically designed to handle and integrate multimodal inputs like images.

nodes.label: Generate Multimodal Instruction
nodes.title: GenerateEnhancedMultimodalInstructionFromFeedback
nodes.description: Creates improved instructions for multimodal tasks by incorporating feedback on visual analysis, textual integration, and domain-specific knowledge.

nodes.label: Fine-tune LM with Reinforcement Learning
nodes.title: GRPO
nodes.description: A reinforcement learning-based optimizer that fine-tunes language models by collecting program execution trajectories and assigning rewards.

nodes.label: Induce Natural Language Rules
nodes.title: InferRules
nodes.description: Discovers and integrates natural language rules from successful examples into program instructions to enhance performance and consistency.

nodes.label: Generate Rules from Examples
nodes.title: CustomRulesInduction
nodes.description: Extracts concise and actionable natural language rules from a set of provided examples to guide program behavior.

nodes.label: Select Few-Shot Demos (KNN)
nodes.title: KNNFewShot
nodes.description: Selects the k-nearest neighbor examples from a training set at inference time to dynamically provide relevant few-shot demonstrations to a program.

nodes.label: Optimize Prompts with Bayesian Search
nodes.title: MIPROv2
nodes.description: Optimizes program prompts and few-shot example selection using Bayesian optimization (Optuna) to find the best performing configurations.

nodes.label: Self-Reflect & Improve Program
nodes.title: SIMBA
nodes.description: A stochastic optimizer that uses LLM self-reflection to analyze program performance, generate improvement rules, or add successful demonstrations.

nodes.label: Append Improvement Rule
nodes.title: append_a_rule
nodes.description: A SIMBA strategy that generates and appends a new natural language rule to a program's instructions based on performance analysis.

nodes.label: Append Few-Shot Demonstration
nodes.title: append_a_demo_
nodes.description: A SIMBA strategy that adds a successful example as a few-shot demonstration to a program's predictors.

nodes.label: Generate Module Feedback
nodes.title: OfferFeedback
nodes.description: Analyzes contrasting program trajectories (better vs. worse) to generate specific, actionable feedback for individual modules.

nodes.label: Optimize Few-Shot Demos with Optuna
nodes.title: BootstrapFewShotWithOptuna
nodes.description: Combines few-shot bootstrapping with Optuna to optimize the selection of demonstrations for a program.

nodes.label: Capture Program Trace & Handle Errors
nodes.title: patched_forward
nodes.description: Patches a program's forward pass to capture execution traces and gracefully handle parsing errors, providing detailed information for optimization.

nodes.label: Language Model
nodes.title: dspy.LM
nodes.description: Core component for interacting with large language models, used by various optimizers for prompt generation, reflection, or task execution.

nodes.label: Program Evaluator
nodes.title: dspy.Evaluate
nodes.description: A utility for evaluating DSPy programs against a dataset using a specified metric, crucial for measuring optimization progress.

nodes.label: Text Embedder
nodes.title: dspy.Embedder
nodes.description: Generates vector representations of text, used by KNNFewShot to find similar examples for few-shot prompting.

nodes.label: Bayesian Optimizer (Optuna)
nodes.title: Optuna
nodes.description: An open-source hyperparameter optimization framework, used by MIPROv2 and BootstrapFewShotWithOptuna for efficient search.

nodes.label: Data Adapter
nodes.title: dspy.Adapter
nodes.description: Handles the formatting and conversion of data for language models, particularly for fine-tuning in GRPO.

nodes.label: Parsing Error Handler
nodes.title: AdapterParseError
nodes.description: An exception raised when an LM's output fails to parse according to the expected signature, handled during trace capture.

nodes.label: Few-Shot Bootstrapping
nodes.title: BootstrapFewShot
nodes.description: A teleprompter that generates few-shot demonstrations by running a teacher model on training examples.

groups.label: Instruction Refinement
groups.title: Instruction Refinement
groups.description: Components focused on iteratively generating and refining program instructions and rules based on performance feedback.

groups.label: Evolutionary & Multimodal Prompting
groups.title: Evolutionary & Multimodal Prompting
groups.description: Optimizers that use evolutionary algorithms and reflection, including specialized components for multimodal instruction generation.

groups.label: Few-Shot & Demo Optimizers
groups.title: Few-Shot & Demo Optimizers
groups.description: Components dedicated to selecting, managing, and optimizing few-shot demonstrations for improved program performance.

groups.label: Advanced & Meta Optimizers
groups.title: Advanced & Meta Optimizers
groups.description: Higher-level optimizers that combine multiple strategies or employ sophisticated search techniques like Bayesian optimization and self-reflection.

groups.label: Reinforcement Learning Fine-tuning
groups.title: Reinforcement Learning Fine-tuning
groups.description: An optimizer that fine-tunes language models using reinforcement learning principles, leveraging program execution trajectories and rewards.

groups.label: Trace & Error Handling
groups.title: Trace & Error Handling
groups.description: Internal utility for capturing program execution traces and managing parsing errors during optimization processes.
